newsitem.title: USA: S&P says rumors of imminent Italy downgrade untrue.
newsitem.headline: S&P says rumors of imminent Italy downgrade untrue.

text.p: Standard & Poor's on Friday said there is no truth to rumors in the Italian bond market that it has issued a statement regarding intentions to change Italy's AA foreign currency rating.
Guido Cipriani, director in S&P's sovereign ratings group, said the rating's negative outlook, which has stood for more than two years, does not signify imminent downgrade risk.
"Imminent risks we signal through the CreditWatch tool, so these are more fundamental underlying credit stories that we're telling with (a negative outlook.)"

Cipriani said rumors probably developed following "fairly bad" news this week from France and Germany in regard to prospects for the European Monetary Union; approval of a three-year Italian budget plan that may signify a slackening of fiscal efforts; and economic data that continues to show weak Italian gross domestic product.

"That together with a general pessimism about Europe this week probably all conspired together to push those rumors forward, but certainly there's no truth to S&P's contribution to that," he said. "We haven't issued anything at all on Italy and we'll stand by the original statement."

Cipriani stressed that S&P is never in a position to divulge when specific actions are being taken, but reiterated there has been no action on the agency's part to change the rating or reasons to feel "particularly concerned at this time."
